content:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx and request timeouts for hosted inference (us-west-2). Threshold crossed: 5xx > 3% for 5m. Paging jamie (oncall).

jamie (oncall): I'm on it — thanks. Pulling logs and starting mitigation runbook.

ashley (sre): saw the spike. There was a spike in KV cache eviction on nodes serving gpt-small-quant. Rolling a throttled rollout to divert to gpt-small-std as fallback.

jamie (oncall): good. Can you confirm expected RPS during fallback and whether latency SLO will be impacted?

ashley (sre): fallback increases p50 ~ 30ms and p95 ~ 120ms. Throughput drop ~8% at peak. Most tails resolved once throttled rollout completed.

devon (prod): we should protect critical customers by routing to Dedicated pools where possible. I'm starting policy for customer-tier routing now.

jamie (oncall): noted. I'm going to update status page draft after we have an initial mitigation summary. Sofia, FYI this may hit customers in batch processing windows. Could be compensation-eligible depending on duration/impact.

sofia (cs): copying here. I'll prepare a holding message for customers and start triaging premium customers. Which metrics should we use to decide eligibility?

mike (billing): from previous playbook, eligibility criteria: 1) sustained error rate > 1% for > 30m or 2) distinct degraded throughput affecting > 10% of requests for > 60m. Need exact windows and affected customer lists to compute credits.

jamie (oncall): we have a sustained window from 2078754300 -> 2078757000 where 5xx averaged ~3.8% across the cluster, with a concentrated hit between 2078754400-2078755800.

ashley (sre): adding details: root cause likely an autoscaler bug that over-evicted cache during a burst. Patch applied at 2078756400, nodes gradually recovered by 2078757600.

jamie (oncall): so total degraded period ~20m heavy, ~40m partial. mike, with those windows, do we meet the billing criteria?

mike (billing): initial calc: weighted impact ~45 minutes above threshold for affected customers. That crosses the 30m threshold for a small credit. We'll need per-customer impact to calculate exact credit amounts. I'll take the per-customer request logs after this thread.

sofia (cs): can we get a list of customers with >5% of their requests impacted? I'll start drafting outreach for those customers once we have the list. Prefer to coordinate messaging before any public status page update.

jamie (oncall): status page draft below (internal only). Please review.

```
Status update (internal draft):
- Incident: Elevated 5xx and timeouts affecting hosted inference in us-west-2
- Impact: Some requests returned 5xx or timed out, impacting approximately X% of total requests between 2078754400 and 2078755800, with recovery beginning at 2078756400.
- Mitigation: Throttled rollout to fallback model, applied autoscaler fix at 2078756400. Ongoing verification.
- Customer action: None required. We are prioritizing Dedicated customer routing and preparing targeted notifications for affected accounts.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or when new information available.
```

jamie (oncall): comments?

devon (prod): add "potential credit assessment underway" and avoid giving amounts. Also mention customers can reach support if they see anomalies.

sofia (cs): agree. Also add a line: "If you believe you are impacted, please open a ticket with sample request IDs and timeframe."

olga (legal): avoid wording that admits contractual breach. Use "service disruption" and "we are assessing eligibility for service credits under customer agreements." Don't promise credits.

jamie (oncall): updated. New draft for public status (short):

```
We are investigating elevated error rates and timeouts affecting hosted inference in us-west-2. Mitigations are in place; recovery is in progress. We are assessing customer impact and eligibility for service credits under customer agreements. Updates will follow here.
```

sofia (cs): thanks. I'll hold on sending customer emails until we have the per-customer impact table from ops. For premium customers, I'll do one-to-one outreach with a personalized note and offer a follow-up call.

mike (billing): next steps for credit calc: ops to provide CSV with columns (customer_id, total_requests, affected_requests, start_ts, end_ts). I'll run the credit formula and return a proposed credit amount and ledger entries.

ashley (sre): exporting logs now. Note: logs will include a spike of 5xx tied to eviction events; we can filter by model and node pool. I'll push CSV to /shared/incidents/2078754321/impact.csv once ready.

jamie (oncall): schedule: ops export ETA 15m. billing calc ETA 30m after that. cs will draft customer language once they get the list.

sofia (cs): drafting two templates: one for affected customers and one for broader notice. Template for affected customers (internal draft):

```
Hi {{customer_name}},

We wanted to let you know about a service disruption in us-west-2 on {{date}} between {{start}} and {{end}} that affected some inference requests. We are sorry for the impact. Our engineers have applied mitigation and services have recovered.

We are assessing whether your account is eligible for a service credit under your agreement and will reach back shortly with details. If you'd like to discuss impact, I'm happy to arrange a call.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference Team
```

sofia (cs): will tailor for premium accounts to include next steps and offer credits proactively once billing confirms amounts.

olga (legal): add a line to avoid language that could create waiver of rights: "This communication does not alter the terms of your agreement."

sofia (cs): added.

mike (billing): got the CSV from /shared/incidents/2078754321/impact.csv. Running calculations now. Will post summary table here when done.

(10m passes)

mike (billing): summary: 12 customers saw >10% of their requests affected for >30m. Proposed credits range from $50 to $6,400 based on our credit schedule. Total estimated run = $22,150. I'll prepare journal entries and request approvals.

sofia (cs): numbers look reasonable. I'll queue outreach for the 12 customers and include the proposed credit amount in the note, per legal guidance ("assessing eligibility" -> once approved we can commit).

olga (legal): approvals required: finance sign-off on amounts and a brief legal note on wording. I'll review the customer notes and approve final wording before send.

jamie (oncall): closing loop: incident resolved and recovered by 2078757600. Root fix deployed to autoscaler at 2078756400. Postmortem owners: ashley + devon. Postmortem ETA 48 hours.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to "resolved" by jamie (oncall).

jamie (oncall): I'll assign postmortem and include a section for customer credit calculation methodology and timeline to notify customers. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
